# PDF fixtures

Checked-in binaries, so their provenance lives here. Two of the three are
produced by tools outside this package on purpose: extracting text from a PDF
that Syncfusion also wrote would only prove its reader agrees with its writer.

Regenerate from the repository root.

## `text_layer.pdf` — a normal PDF with a text layer

Printed by CUPS (macOS), the way a real "Save as PDF" would be. One page, a
few lines of prose padded out with the trailing spaces a printed page carries.

```bash
printf 'Caverno PDF fixture\n\nThe quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\nSecond page marker follows.\n' > /tmp/sample.txt
cupsfilter /tmp/sample.txt > test/fixtures/pdf/text_layer.pdf
```

## `image_only.pdf` — a scanned document

A 64x64 PNG wrapped in a PDF, so the page parses but yields no characters.
This is the `noTextLayer` case: the file parsed, but no characters came out.

```bash
sips -s format pdf /tmp/scan.png --out test/fixtures/pdf/image_only.pdf
```

Any small PNG works; the one used here was a generated gradient.

## `ascii_uncompressed.pdf` — a PDF that reads as plain text

Hand-built with no compressed streams, so every byte is printable ASCII and a
UTF-8 sniff classifies the whole file as text. This is the fixture that proves
`read_file` asks "is this a PDF?" before it asks "is this binary?" — with the
checks in the other order it would return raw `%PDF` syntax to the model.

Generated by `python3` with no dependencies: five objects (catalog, pages,
page, an uncompressed content stream drawing one line of Helvetica, and the
font), followed by a hand-computed xref table and trailer. Regenerate it by
writing that structure out again; the only property that matters is that no
byte falls outside printable ASCII plus tab/CR/LF.

## `encrypted.pdf` — password-protected

Written with `syncfusion_flutter_pdf` (user password `caverno`, owner password
`caverno-owner`) because nothing else on a stock macOS box encrypts a PDF. The
reader path under test never decrypts it, so the writer being the same library
buys it nothing here.

```dart
final document = PdfDocument();
document.security
  ..userPassword = 'caverno'
  ..ownerPassword = 'caverno-owner';
document.pages.add().graphics.drawString(
  'Locked fixture body text.',
  PdfStandardFont(PdfFontFamily.helvetica, 12),
  bounds: const Rect.fromLTWH(20, 20, 400, 40),
);
File('test/fixtures/pdf/encrypted.pdf').writeAsBytesSync(await document.save());
document.dispose();
```
